title: War Council — Editor Intro
summary: Editorial opening splash that re-arms the live pressures entering Issue 11 without revealing later issue payoffs.
settingText: Apartment 5B table with municipal review notice, morning
panelPlan: Full-page editorial/title splash around the household table after the review notice arrives. Five adults occupy the room in distinct postures and distances; Carrie has the notice, but nobody is visually arranged behind Bjorn as a unit he commands.
The apartment should feel unmistakably like home now. The new pressure is classification, not whether they belong in the room.
Use table edge, wall space and the official notice as caption anchors. The phrase "'we' may not be enough" should sit over a composition that visibly contains five separate people.
Do not show Gunnar's later object demonstration, anyone's specific answer about the future, Silas's help, rehearsal refusals, or hearing evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: New York once needed one answer for five people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the city is reconsidering the arrangement.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: What each of them wants may be something else entirely.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow they go into a room where 'we' may not be enough.

title: The Notice
summary: An ordinary morning becomes vulnerable when Carrie recognizes a municipal Status Reconciliation Review notice in the building mail.
settingText: Bushwick building mailboxes and apartment 5B, morning
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie sorts ordinary mail while balancing coffee and a folder. A thick DTI envelope is mixed among routine envelopes.
Insert: Only the required notice header is readable: STATUS RECONCILIATION REVIEW.
Close on Carrie: Her expression changes.
Wide: Inside 5B, breakfast is underway when Carrie enters holding the paper too carefully.
Two-shot: Bjorn reads Carrie's face before the document.

dialogueInline.text: Now the city is reconsidering the arrangement.
Us. In a room. Answering questions.

title: War Council
summary: Bjorn responds to the review by clearing the table, while Gunnar immediately questions whether one household can provide one answer.
panelPlan: Wide overhead-ish table: Bjorn clears cups and books with ceremonial seriousness. Carrie places the notice down. Gunnar brings coffee. The two male Kin sit nearby; Astrid is already out.
Insert: Bjorn places the brass apartment key in the center of the table.
Medium: Bjorn plants both hands beside the key.
Medium: Carrie keeps one finger on the dense review notice, trying to identify the actual questions.
Medium: Gunnar sits with coffee, not a map.

dialogueInline.text: First I need to know what they're actually reviewing.
First we should know what we mean by household.
That may not be what they mean.

directionInline.text: Astrid is off-page by ordinary routine, not because of danger or estrangement.

title: Four Things
summary: Gunnar separates home, city access, legal status and kinship into different categories, making the household's hidden assumptions visible.
panelPlan: Medium: Bjorn gestures around the room as if the definition should be obvious.
Insert: Gunnar touches the brass key.
Insert: He points to a transit card, the review notice and a shared wooden bowl in turn.
Two-shot: The four objects remain physically separated on the table.
Close on Bjorn: He studies the separation.

dialogueInline.text: Card is the city. Paper is status. Bowl is us.
Same life. Not the same thing.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Different Answers
summary: The household immediately refuses one collective answer: First Male Kin wants the room and block, while Second Male Kin is less certain.
panelPlan: Top-down insert: key, transit card, notice and bowl.
Medium: First Male Kin points to key and bowl.
Medium: Second Male Kin points to the transit card, then hesitates over the key.
Close on Bjorn: His old reflex to unify the answer appears.
Medium: Carrie stops him before he completes it.

dialogueInline.text: I don't know every home I will ever want.
He does not know where he will live later.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: What Changes
summary: First Male Kin asks the practical question beneath the review: whether the hearing can take away the ordinary life he already has.
panelPlan: Medium: First Male Kin keeps one hand near the brass key rather than the notice.
Two-shot: He asks Carrie what a bad review actually changes.
Medium: Carrie distinguishes immediate housing from longer-term legal status without promising an outcome.
Close on Bjorn: He hears the uncertainty.
Wide: Nobody reaches for the key.

dialogueInline.text: If they say no, do we lose the room?
Could they make us leave New York?
Not because of one answer. But status changes what becomes harder later.
Keeping the room does not settle permanent status.
Wanting this room is enough for that part.
Wanting this room does not decide the rest.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: For Now
summary: Second Male Kin can say he likes New York without promising a permanent future he cannot honestly know.
panelPlan: Medium: Second Male Kin turns the transit card between his fingers.
Medium: Bjorn waits rather than finishing his thought.
Close: Second Male Kin looks toward the apartment window while answering.
Medium: Carrie gives him the institutional question without pushing permanence.
Two-shot: Bjorn accepts the present-tense answer.

dialogueInline.text: I don't know if I want only New York.
I don't know. That is why only is too large.
They'll ask if you plan to stay.
That's actually a pretty good answer.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Gunnar's Answer
summary: Gunnar's reasons for staying are now chosen interests rather than survival tasks, but he still resists converting them into a permanent declaration.
panelPlan: Medium: Gunnar closes the library book beside his coffee.
Two-shot: Bjorn asks what Gunnar would answer.
Medium: Gunnar names ordinary chosen things.
Close on Carrie: She listens rather than translating.
Wide: The review notice remains untouched while Gunnar's book stays open nearby.

dialogueInline.text: Books. Coffee. The park when it isn't full of children.
Maybe I don't need a reason for forever.
They aren't asking for poetry. They're asking intent.
Then my intent is breakfast tomorrow and the library after.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: They Do Not Match
summary: Bjorn confronts the fact that five adults can share a household without sharing one answer about the future.
panelPlan: Wide: The four objects remain on the table while everyone occupies a different posture around them.
Medium: Bjorn looks from First Male Kin to Gunnar to Second Male Kin.
Close: He states the problem as he sees it.
Medium: Carrie refuses to treat difference as a defect.
Two-shot: Gunnar makes the obvious point.

dialogueInline.text: We survived because we moved as one.
And now you don't have to.
Then moving as one ends here.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Four Questions
summary: Carrie reduces the dense review notice to four actual categories: residence, independence, intent and household ties.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie turns the review notice around toward the group.
Insert: Only four required category labels are legible: RESIDENCE, INDEPENDENCE, INTENT, HOUSEHOLD TIES.
Medium: Gunnar counts them on his fingers.
Close on Bjorn: Four questions are easier to confront than a page of institutional language.
Wide: Carrie pushes the rest of the notice aside.

dialogueInline.text: Four categories pretending to be questions.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Residence
summary: The easiest category is still not identical to home: all five live at 5B, but Carrie warns that residence is a legal fact, not a statement about belonging.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie taps RESIDENCE on the notice.
Wide: Everyone can physically see the same room around them.
Two-shot: Bjorn calls the answer obvious.
Medium: Carrie confirms the address while drawing the distinction.
Close on Gunnar: He repeats the distinction in simpler terms.

dialogueInline.text: Residence is easy. You live here.
Address is obvious. What the address means is not.
Where we sleep is not the same as why we stay.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Independence
summary: Carrie explains that independence does not mean living without help, which prevents the household from mistaking mutual reliance for legal dependency.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie taps INDEPENDENCE.
Close: Bjorn immediately dislikes the word.
Two-shot: Carrie explains that the review is asking whether each adult can act and decide for themselves, not whether they never rely on anyone.
Medium: First Male Kin points toward the shared kitchen and laundry.
Wide: The group sees that mutual household work does not answer the legal question.

dialogueInline.text: Can each of you make decisions, go places, handle ordinary life, ask for help when you need it?

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Intent
summary: The intent category creates exactly the problem Second Male Kin anticipated: institutions ask future questions from people who can only answer honestly in the present.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie taps INTENT.
Close on Second Male Kin: He already knows why this one is difficult.
Two-shot: Carrie explains the question in plain language.
Medium: Bjorn starts to offer certainty, then stops himself.
Wide: Second Male Kin keeps the answer he actually has.

dialogueInline.text: Intent. Do you plan to remain?

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Household Ties
summary: The final category makes visible the season's central distinction: the household can be real without Bjorn's authority defining everyone inside it.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie taps HOUSEHOLD TIES.
Insert: The shared wooden bowl and brass key sit beside the notice.
Two-shot: Bjorn says the kinship is obvious.
Medium: Carrie explains that the hearing may ask how people rely on one another and who decides what.
Close on Bjorn: He understands why that last part matters.
Wide: Nobody offers him a collective answer.

dialogueInline.text: They may ask what that means in practice.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Silas Has a Campaign
summary: Silas hears about the review and reflexively proposes a public campaign, then realizes he is trying to become narrator again.
panelPlan: Wide: Silas enters or appears at the doorway after hearing about the review, phone already in hand.
Medium: He starts outlining a social-media/public-pressure idea.
Close on Carrie: She shuts it down before he gets momentum.
Two-shot: Gunnar points out that the hearing is asking them, not the public.
Medium: Silas lowers the phone.

dialogueInline.text: We could get ahead of this. Short video. Their own words. People would—
They are already asking our own words.

title: Be Useful

settingText: Bushwick neighborhood print/copy shop and apartment doorway
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie hands Silas two pages and a simple instruction.
Wide: Brief transition to a neighborhood print/copy counter; Silas gets clean copies without filming.
Insert: His phone stays in his pocket.
Medium: Silas returns to 5B with the copies only.
Two-shot: Carrie accepts them.

title: Leave Room for People
summary: Carrie narrows the table to the records actually needed while Bjorn refuses to let symbolic objects stand in for the people who use them.
panelPlan: Top-down: Brass key, transit card, library card, bodega receipt, review notice and a small household tool are scattered across the table.
Medium: Carrie separates required documents from illustrative clutter.
Medium: Bjorn looks past the objects to the people in the room.
Two-shot: Carrie understands the distinction.
Wide: She deliberately clears seats around the table.

dialogueInline.text: This gets us through the door.
The clerk needs paper. The hearing needs people.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: What Do You Want
summary: Bjorn asks the three men what each wants and allows the answers to remain different.
panelPlan: Wide: Bjorn sits with Carrie, Gunnar and the two male Kin; documents are pushed to the side.
Medium: First Male Kin answers from the life he already has around the block.
Medium: Gunnar answers without looking at the notice.
Medium: Second Male Kin gives the present-tense answer again.
Two-shot: Bjorn looks at Carrie rather than forcing synthesis.

dialogueInline.text: The room. This block. People know me here.
Different answers are not a failure.
A household does not need one answer to remain a household.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: No Rehearsal
summary: Carrie refuses to manufacture polished answers for the review; knowing the categories is enough.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie points to the four categories without writing sample answers.
Medium: Gunnar looks from the page to Carrie.
Close: Second Male Kin leans back, visibly relieved not to rehearse certainty.
Two-shot: Bjorn still wants a plan.
Wide: The notice remains partly unanswered.

dialogueInline.text: Bring documents. Tell the truth. That's the plan.
Because you want a battle plan.
Then don't invent answers to make everybody match.

source: Rebuilt War Council after Belonging extracted the separate-routines / independent-city-life material.

title: Sit
summary: Carrie moves from authoring the household's case to explaining procedure at the same table level as everyone else.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie remains standing with the notice while the others sit.
Medium: Bjorn slides the empty chair out with his boot.
Close: Carrie looks at the chair and the partly unanswered notice.
Wide at table height: Carrie sits.
Two-shot: Bjorn pushes the notice toward her, but not the answers.

dialogueInline.text: You are making a wall with the paper.
I can tell you procedure. I can't tell you what to say.
You really don't want me fixing the answers?

title: Astrid Comes Home
summary: Astrid returns from an ordinary independent day; Carrie catches herself before turning the arrival into an intake interview.
panelPlan: Wide: Astrid comes up the stairs carrying a small reusable bag and one folded receipt or paper; the props reveal nothing dramatic.
Medium: Astrid unlocks 5B with her own key.
Two-shot: Carrie reflexively starts to ask where she was, then stops herself.
Wide: Astrid sees the review notice and the gathered household.
Medium: Carrie asks only the question relevant to tomorrow.

dialogueInline.text: Nobody else is answering for me.

title: Ask the Rest
summary: Astrid refuses a rehearsal without being evasive, preserving the hearing's ability to discover the substance of her independent life.
panelPlan: Medium: Carrie asks one obvious preparatory question.
Close on Astrid: She answers only the part she chooses.
Two-shot: Carrie waits for more.
Medium: Bjorn almost follows up, then decides not to.
Wide: Astrid keeps the folded paper to herself and joins the table.

dialogueInline.text: You want to keep this home?
And if they ask how independent—

title: Borrowed Answers
summary: Second Male Kin worries that the review will demand certainty about a future he does not have; Bjorn no longer tries to lend him certainty.

Two-shot: Bjorn joins him without blocking the window or route back to the room.

Medium: She clips only the required records together.

Medium: Silas hands over his two clean printer copies, phone still pocketed.

dialogueInline.text: IDs. Residence. Notices. What they require.

title: My Part
summary: The household ends the night without a shared script; Bjorn accepts that tomorrow each adult must answer for themselves.
panelPlan: Wide: The table is mostly clear. Gunnar closes a book. The two male Kin separate into evening routines. Astrid puts away her small bag. Carrie stands to leave.
Insert: The brass key remains near the closed hearing file; no collective statement sits beside it.
Medium: Carrie pauses at the doorway.
Medium on Bjorn: He looks from the closed file to the people around the room.
